item.title: Xi says positive interaction between major countries not an option but a must
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Xi says positive interaction between major countries not an option but a must SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that positive interaction between major countries is "not optional, but a must." Xi made the remarks at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. "Humanity, living in the same global village, is a community with a shared future where we all stand to benefit or lose together. In this global village, major countries shoulder special responsibilities," he said. In recent years, China has been promoting the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era, and actively developing the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, with a view to fostering major-country dynamics featuring peaceful coexistence, overall stability, and balanced development to the benefit of each other and the world at large, he said. Noting that transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe, Xi said the world is not peaceful and testing times reveal responsibilities on one's shoulders. As major countries and permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, China, Russia and the United States should set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make greater contributions to the progress of humanity. item.title: Xi makes four points on how major countries should get along with each other
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Xi makes four points on how major countries should get along with each other SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace. Major countries should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation, Xi said at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Xi said that countries should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respect the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns. They should not interfere in other countries' domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs, he said. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another, Xi said. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should be partners and friends. They should not go for conflict or confrontation among themselves, but should hold the line on peaceful coexistence and make efforts to avoid the Thucydides Trap. As the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, Xi said. He said that nuclear weapons, the Sword of Damocles that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons. He emphasized the importance of win-win cooperation. The three countries should strengthen economic cooperation and trade, combine their respective strengths as major countries in resources, manufacturing and consumption, so as to make the pie of cooperation bigger and achieve win-win and all-win outcomes. Decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains are not the way to go. Xi said that the three countries could strengthen communication and coordination to safeguard the security and stability of the global energy market. He said that the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms to ensure that misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means. item.title: China is advocate, promoter, forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation: Xi
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
China is advocate, promoter, forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation: Xi Chinese President Xi Jinping chairs the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and delivers important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday said China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, and it is ready to work with all parties to build the pillars that support an Asia-Pacific community. Xi made the remarks at the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen in south China's Guangdong Province. Stressing the importance of stronger economic and trade ties underpinning such a community, Xi said efforts should be made to facilitate trade and investment, advance digitalization, and lower barriers to them. On upgrading connectivity, he called for measures to improve infrastructure networks, enhance coordination in policies and regulations, promote people-to-people exchanges, and foster mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Emphasizing innovation, Xi said greater efforts need to be made to build digital infrastructure and promote the broad application of artificial intelligence. Xi stressed the importance of development, calling on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also called for efforts to improve the people's well-being and increase investment in human capital. Chinese President Xi Jinping poses for a group photo with leaders and representatives from other economies before the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. Xi chaired the meeting and delivered important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" on Thursday. item.title: Full text: China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Full text: China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- The following is the full text of the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, released on Thursday. China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace Xi Jinping, President of the People's Republic of China, Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation, and Donald J. Trump, President of the United States of America, met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. The Russian and U.S. heads of state expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic trilateral Summit. The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security. 1. As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, China, Russia, and the United States committed to reform the U.N. so that the U.N. can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security. 2. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. 3. The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. 4. The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi urges actively addressing population aging
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Xi urges actively addressing population aging BEIJING, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged further efforts to implement the national strategy of actively addressing population aging and to ensure happier and more fulfilling lives for elderly people. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on work related to aging. Since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in 2012, China has made fresh progress in responding to population aging, with both elderly care services and the elderly care industry developing at a rapid pace, Xi said. Xi emphasized the importance of coordinating efforts among the government, market, society and families and further strengthening social security, elderly care services, health services, and social participation for older people. He also stressed the need to boost the silver economy and build an age-friendly society. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a national meeting on aging held from Wednesday to Thursday in Beijing. Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, attended and delivered a speech at the meeting. Li stressed the need to take a balanced perspective on the far-reaching implications of an aging population, be fully aware of China's unique advantages in addressing this demographic shift, and act with a stronger sense of responsibility and greater proactivity to advance work in this area. With the goal of enhancing the wellbeing of elderly people, efforts should be made to meet their needs for a better life and deliver on key tasks concerning elderly people, Li said. China has the world's largest elderly population. By the end of 2025, China had 323.38 million people aged 60 and above, or 23 percent of the population. The figure is projected to exceed 400 million by around 2035. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Peng Liyuan, spouses of APEC economies' leaders visit cultural exhibition
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Peng Liyuan, spouses of APEC economies' leaders visit cultural exhibition SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, and spouses of leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies visited a cultural exhibition on Thursday in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Peng warmly greeted the guests at the Shenzhen Bay Culture Square. They watched a festive and vibrant Xingshi (awakening lion) performance and the Yingge dance presented by a group of children, and visited the exhibition showcasing efforts to preserve and pass on local intangible cultural heritage. During the visit, they viewed with interest exquisite handicrafts, enjoyed an artistic performance featuring Lingnan culture and experienced a digital presentation of local arcade streets. Peng told the guests that Lingnan culture, an important part of Chinese culture, embodies the wisdom of harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature. China is willing to enhance cultural exchanges and mutual learning with the rest of the world, she said. The guests spoke highly of the long history and richness of traditional Chinese culture and achievements in advancing Chinese modernization. They also expressed their willingness to enhance exchanges and cooperation with China. At the end of the visit, Peng and the guests posed for a group photo. Participating in Thursday's activities included wives of Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, President of the Republic of Korea Lee Jae Myung, Philippine President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr., and General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam. item.title: Xi meets Trump, calling for continued efforts to steer China-U.S. relations on right course
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Xi meets Trump, calling for continued efforts to steer China-U.S. relations on right course Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with U.S. President Donald Trump, who is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday in Shenzhen, calling for continued efforts to jointly steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relations in the right direction toward the future. Trump is in the southern Chinese city for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. During the meeting, Xi said that China-U.S. relations have generally maintained a stable and positive trajectory, bringing tangible benefits to people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world. Xi said that he and Trump had jointly explored the right way for China and the United States, as two major countries, to get along, established a new vision to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and given it new substance grounded in respect, fairness and reciprocity. The new vision has been welcomed by the people of both China and the United States, as well as the international community, he added. Xi stressed that building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented and pioneering endeavor, adding that the key to sustaining the current positive momentum lies in taking concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state. The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. Xi called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns, and work toward mutual benefit. The cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness, and reciprocity. China and the United States should strengthen communication and coordination to guard against security risks of artificial intelligence (AI) and ensure that AI always remains under human control, he said. On the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-U.S. relations, Xi said. Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of U.S.-China relations, adding that both leaders have maintained close contact, with their friendship growing stronger. Trade and investment ties between the two countries have continued to grow, and cooperation on fentanyl and other issues has yielded results, Trump noted. He called on both sides to maintain the positive momentum of the stable development in bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation in areas such as farm products, energy and super intelligence. The United States does not support "Taiwan independence," Trump said. He congratulated China on hosting a successful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, adding that both countries need to work together to lead and promote world peace and stability. item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Xi Focus: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community Chinese President Xi Jinping chairs the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and delivers important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam. item.title: China-Russia-U.S. summit positive, constructive, fruitful: Xi
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
China-Russia-U.S. summit positive, constructive, fruitful: Xi SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that the China-Russia-U.S. summit has been positive, constructive and fruitful. Xi made the remarks while summarizing main consensus reached at the summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The three countries share the same view on safeguarding world peace, and all stressed that the hard-won peace must be cherished, Xi said. They all agree that major countries should take the legitimate security concerns of every country seriously and that dialogue and negotiation are the right choice to resolve differences, Xi said. "There is hope for peace as long as dialogue does not cease and the door does not close," Xi said. They also agreed that cooperation is essential to overcoming challenges, Xi said. The three countries should follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, continue to strengthen communication, promote peace through cooperation, and work together to build a better world. item.title: Xi hosts welcome banquet for guests attending APEC meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Xi hosts welcome banquet for guests attending APEC meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping addresses a welcome banquet in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday hosted a banquet in Shenzhen to welcome guests who are here to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei) SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday hosted a banquet in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, to welcome guests who are here to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. "I wish to extend, on behalf of the Chinese government and the Chinese people, our warmest welcome to all distinguished guests," Xi said in his toast. Openness is deeply rooted in Shenzhen's DNA and innovation drives the city's vitality, while cooperation is where its strength comes from, Xi said, adding that the success of Shenzhen is also a microcosm of China's reform and opening up, as well as an example of fruitful cooperation across the Asia-Pacific. Noting that openness, innovation and cooperation have been the distinctive features of APEC since its establishment, Xi said APEC has grasped the pulse of the times and guided the process of regional economic integration, making the Asia-Pacific the most dynamic region and a vital growth engine of the world economy. "At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss steps to expand mutual openness, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, extend opportunities for result-oriented cooperation across various fields," Xi said. Before the banquet, Xi and Peng posed for group photos with leaders and representatives from APEC economies and their spouses.
